name: Erythrokeratoderma en cocardes

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and histopathological diagnostic criteria for erythrokeratoderma en cocardes

criteria.description: Presence of well-demarcated, erythematous, hyperkeratotic plaques with characteristic concentric or targetoid (en cocardes) morphology
Skin biopsy showing hyperkeratosis, acanthosis, and papillomatosis without significant inflammation
Identification of mutations in connexin genes (GJB3 or GJB4) associated with erythrokeratoderma

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical lesions plus supportive histopathology; genetic testing supports diagnosis but is not mandatory
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by histopathology; genetic confirmation is helpful but not always available.

laboratory: Skin biopsy showing hyperkeratosis, acanthosis, and papillomatosis without significant inflammation
genetic: Mutations in connexin genes GJB3 and GJB4 identified by molecular genetic testing
other: Clinical observation of characteristic targetoid plaques

distinguishingFeatures: Transient migratory erythematous patches rather than fixed plaques
Progressive course with less defined concentric rings

redFlags: Rapid progression of skin lesions with ulceration
Signs of systemic infection secondary to skin barrier breakdown
Development of severe palmoplantar keratoderma impairing function
references: Happle R. Erythrokeratodermas: a review. Dermatology. 1997;194(3):193-9.
Richard G, et al. Connexin mutations in erythrokeratodermia variabilis and related disorders. Am J Hum Genet. 1998.
